narrative.overview: Endroit presents itself as a bound book of numbered multi-part forms. A pressboard binding holds sheets of form stock, and the stock colour names the party whose authority a section is about: bond for the shipper who directs and signs, canary for the carrier that runs the agent, blue for the consignee Site that owns its own destination.
keyCharacteristics: Stock colour is semantic: it names the party, never the rhythm.
Type is semantic: pre-printed, filled-in and stamped are three distinct registers.
Mechanisms appear as records (manifest lines, ledger states, stamps), not as illustrations of records.
No webfont, no client framework, no third-party request; the whole argument reads with JavaScript off.

rules.name: Stock Names the Party
rules.body: Never choose a stock for rhythm. If a section is not about the carrier or the consignee, it prints on bond.

rules.name: Verbatim Identifier
rules.body: A version, path or protocol id inside pre-printed matter resets text-transform and letter-spacing; casing must never rewrite 0.10.0-alpha.0.

rules.name: Bounded Board
rules.body: The binding may be the page ground, the bar, the footer and the audit sheets. Long-form reading always happens on stock.

rules.name: Exclusion Is a Record
rules.body: A not-aboard line keeps full opacity and carries a reason code; it is never a de-emphasised row.

dos: Do print exclusion as legibly as inclusion, with its reason.
Do keep a claim, its mechanism, its proof and its maturity in one record.
Do preserve keyboard completion, visible focus, AA contrast, reduced motion and the full no-JavaScript reading.
Do treat 320px as a first-class printing of the same form set.
donts: Don't use a stock, an oxide mark or a green seal without the meaning it names.
Don't add a fake terminal, an IDE frame, a node graph, a decorative dashboard, a purple gradient or an all-dark developer template.
Don't let pre-printed casing rewrite a version string, path or protocol id.
Don't hide a product claim behind an interaction, or imply automatic memory, silent retention, an any-agent guarantee or a measured productivity gain.
